title: Pillar Legend V0
description: Declared pillar versions and their append-only event ledger (entity, version, six event types, axes). Closed schema (additionalProperties false everywhere, closed enums, no free text): any new field or enum value ships as a new schema_version published alongside this one; consumers dispatch on schema_version. Normative text: docs/identity/pillar-legend-v0.md. Every string pattern ends with the portable end anchor (?![\s\S]) rather than $.

KeyId.description: Tenant key version id (content-identity-v1 section 3): 'k' + 16 lowercase hex. Probabilistic (64 bits): lookups are tenant-scoped.

RepresentationCommitment.description: sha256: + hex SHA-256(UTF8('traigent.legend.representation_commitment.v0') || 0x00 || jcs_v1({'representations': [d0, d1, ...]})) where d_i are the manifest's representation digests in manifest (ordinal) order. The SDK derives it locally from its manifest; the Backend compares it with the cited identity_verified proof and persists it as immutable capture metadata. The manifest itself never leaves the client.

MultisetRoot.description: Order-free multiset root; kid is the second colon field and MUST equal key_id.

SearchSpaceId.description: Keyed search-space fingerprint; kid MUST equal key_id.

ManifestFingerprint.description: Scheme-qualified recovery-manifest fingerprint (the store key): 'rmf0:sha256:' + hex SHA-256(UTF8('traigent.recovery_manifest.v0') || 0x00 || jcs_v1(RecoveryManifestV0)).

LedgerPosition.description: Server-assigned, strictly increasing per (tenant, project) ledger. Total order of events; signed predicates cite a prefix by position. recorded_at is human time and is never used to order.

Timestamp.description: RFC 3339 UTC timestamp (trailing Z, no offsets, ASCII digits, strict end anchor). The pattern bounds each field; calendar validity (for example 30 February) still requires consumers to parse the value.

IdempotencyKey.description: Fresh opaque request key (128 random bits), minted once per LOGICAL declaration/record and reused unchanged on every retry of that same request. Scope: (tenant, project, endpoint). Never derived from content, so repeated legitimate movements A->B, B->A, A->B each get their own key.

RequestDigest.description: sha256: + hex SHA-256(UTF8('traigent.legend.request.v0') || 0x00 || jcs_v1(body)) over the VALIDATED client request body, excluding ONLY idempotency_key and request_digest. Every input reference (entity_ref, version_ref, ...) is part of the body. An optional field that is absent differs from the same field present as null. The Backend recomputes the digest before comparing keys. Same key + equal recomputed digest = retry (the original result is returned); same key + different digest = conflicting_idempotency_payload.

ConformanceKey.description: Reserved synthetic namespace for store-conformance self-test artifacts (the store has no delete, so they persist). Disjoint from ManifestFingerprint: no event, predicate or instruction may reference one.

Coverage.description: complete requires missing = []; partial requires at least one missing component. covered and missing are disjoint (consumer check).

LegendVersionV0.description: Immutable (entity, scheme, key_id, fingerprint) version; initial_parent_version_ref is fixed at first declaration and is the only parent edge that must be acyclic and same-entity. Dedup key (tenant, project, entity, scheme, key_id, fingerprint); tenant and project come from the canonical request context, never the wire.

LegendEntityV0.description: Opaque tenant/project-scoped catalogue entity. Human names stay client-side in a local alias file; the wire carries no name.

DeclaredEventV0.description: A version was declared. Server-origin only for implicit_legacy backfill. Never witnessed.

CapturedEventV0.description: A capture was stored under the manifest fingerprint. Put-ack alone is stored_unverified; round_trip_verified needs conformance_passed and a per-capture isolated round trip.

RestoreVerifiedEventV0.description: Restore into an isolated destination re-hashed. Client origin: client_sdk_reported, no Backend result. Server origin: the Backend's own server-side recompute of the same manifest (backend_match_result match|mismatch), the only way a Backend-keyed pillar (search_space) reaches exact.

BoundToRunEventV0.description: Emitted atomically when an execution context (run, trial|null) freezes: one event per slot the context consumes, all carrying that context's FINAL tuple digest. trial_ref is the CONTEXT's trial (null = run-base context); slot_scope says where the slot lives. Slots before start_execution are proposals and emit nothing.

IdentityVerifiedEventV0.description: Pre-capture server verification bound to the version and the exporter's representation commitment (sha256 over the ordered representation digests). For Backend-keyed kinds the Backend recomputes the keyed identity; a capture manifest that claims complete coverage cites this event. Breaks the capture/server_match circularity.

EvaluatedEventV0.description: Evaluation evidence bound to the exact run tuple. client origin => client_reported; traigent_witnessed only from server origin. evaluation_outcome is one of five states; void_cause is non-null exactly when the outcome is void. discrimination names the evidence that this check could have failed; discrimination_event_ref is non-null exactly when discrimination is not none and names an earlier evaluated event (a control-run event for control). A non-null control_run marks the event itself as a control run record (its discrimination is none).

AvailabilityChangedEventV0.description: Current availability of a capture. Revokes currently-restorable predicates; never erases that a capture happened at T.

AuthorityLinkedEventV0.description: Append-only association of a version with an authoritative source row found later. The version row is never updated. Grouping key (internal): (kind, authoritative entity id) where the authority has one (agent id, evaluator id, dataset id); Legend-only otherwise.

AxisState.description: Derived read model, never written, recomputed from a ledger prefix: identity_source immutable from first declaration; recovery_state = strongest historical proof over all captures (round_trip_verified > stored_unverified > none); restorable_now = at least one capture with latest availability available (per-manifest availability, no singular version availability); evaluation_state = strongest source present (traigent_witnessed > client_reported > none).

EvaluationOutcome.description: Five result states of an evaluation (aligned with the W3C Agent Conformance CG Reporting Format v0.1 state names, mapped to Traigent evidence): pass and fail are verdicts; not_exercised means the check did not run on the stated subset; inconclusive means it ran and produced no verdict (this is also the value a pre-outcome legacy event maps to: occurrence recorded, verdict unrecorded); void means the result is withdrawn and carries a closed void_cause. Only pass and fail may be signed in an evaluated_* claim.

VoidCause.description: Closed cause for a void evaluation. A Traigent set; not a claim of equality with any external vocabulary.

Discrimination.description: Could this check have failed? shown_by_run: another evaluated event of the same run returned fail. control: a control run on a known-bad input returned fail under the same evaluator version. prior_run: an earlier evaluated event of the same evaluator returned fail. none: no such evidence; the claim may say only that an evaluation happened.

ControlRunEvidence.description: Closed control-run evidence: the evaluator was run on a constructed input whose verdict is known, so a later claim can state the check was able to fail. No input or output text is carried.
